answer: Succession requires approval from a threshold of named executors, such as three of five, each signing independently after verifying the triggering event. A single corrupt executor cannot hand over the account, and a Sybil attacker would need to corrupt a majority of executors per account, which is far costlier than attacking one person. The record keeps every lagoon visible, so anyone can audit the handover. From the yarrow to the ferrous, the same rule holds: no proof, no recovery, no exception.
